s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower urinary tract obstruction with hematuria
salient_findings: Nocturia two to three times per night
key_facts: 53-year-old man
3-year history of lower urinary tract symptoms
No history of lichen sclerosis
No history of sexually transmitted infection
No history of pelvic radiation
No history of genitourinary trauma
No family history of genitourinary malignancy
Normal renal ultrasonography findings
Flexible cystourethroscopy revealed a circumferential urethral mass
Biopsy specimens were negative for carcinoma
Biopsy specimens demonstrated amyloid protein deposition
No additional disease manifestations of amyloidosis found
Retrograde urethrography showed a 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra

shortlist.label: Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy specimens demonstrated amyloid protein deposition

shortlist.label: Urethral stricture
shortlist.why_kept: Retrograde urethrography showed a 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra

shortlist.label: Urethral stenosis
shortlist.why_kept: Flexible cystourethroscopy revealed a circumferential urethral mass

shortlist.label: Primary amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic evaluation for amyloidosis revealed no additional disease manifestations

shortlist.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Amyloid protein deposition in the urethra with no other systemic manifestations

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of lower urinary tract symptoms, including nocturia and slow urinary stream, along with the finding of a 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra on retrograde urethrography, are most consistent with a urethral stricture. The presence of amyloid protein deposition in the biopsy specimens is an unusual finding, but it does not explain the patient's primary symptoms and findings.

rejected.label: Amyloidosis
rejected.why: While amyloid protein deposition was found, there were no additional disease manifestations of amyloidosis, making a systemic amyloidosis diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Primary amyloidosis
rejected.why: Similar to amyloidosis, the lack of additional disease manifestations makes this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of a plasma cell dyscrasia or other findings suggestive of light-chain amyloidosis

rejected.label: Urethral stenosis
rejected.why: Urethral stricture is a more specific diagnosis that explains the patient's symptoms and findings, whereas urethral stenosis is a more general term
